results.question: Were there any early warning signs before the K-301 trip in March 2026?
results.reason: The assistant's answer contains all key facts from the reference answer: it confirms the presence of early warning signs, notes the discharge temperature trending up for at least ten days prior to the trip, and mentions the June 2025 inspection flagging the intercooler approach temperature trending up. The additional details provided are consistent and do not contradict the reference.
results.answer:
Yes, there were clear early warning signs. Compressor K-301's discharge temperature (TI-302) had been rising steadily for at least ten days before the March 3 trip, with the trend visible in operating data. The temperature climbed from 127 °C on February 20 to 142 °C by the trip date, crossing a 135 °C threshold around March 1 [e32d19761eea4940]. No intermediate high-temperature alarm existed at that time to alert operators to the trend [504bb2a40e87251c]. The root cause investigation confirmed the rising discharge temperature was apparent in the trend well before the trip, but it went unaddressed because trend review was not part of the daily operator round checklist and the strainer responsible for cooling water flow degradation was not on any preventive maintenance schedule [504bb2a40e87251c].

An even earlier, subtler indicator was recorded during a June 2025 performance test: the intercooler approach temperature was already trending upward, with a note to monitor [graph path: K-301 GOVERNED_BY OEM date 2025-06-08]. While not the direct cause of the March 2026 trip, it signaled deteriorating heat transfer that could have prompted a closer look at the cooling water side.

results.answer:
Verify suction pressure on PI-102 is at least 0.8 barg before restart, and confirm the suction strainer is clean.  

P-101A has a documented history of seal failures caused by running below the minimum suction pressure specified in SOP-U100-07. The last event (WO-2201) showed PI-102 reading 0.5 barg at start, well under the 0.8 barg minimum, and the pump was weeping at the gland again [7bb5d5e5e90aaeac]. The graph directly links this condition to cavitation: (P-101A) -HAS_FAILURE (cause: running below minimum suction pressure)-> (CAVITATION). Cavitation destroys mechanical seals rapidly, which is why this pump has needed three replacements. The same email also notes that a half-blocked suction strainer was found previously (WO-2257), so verifying strainer condition addresses the root cause of low suction pressure [7bb5d5e5e90aaeac].
